ICD Profile 
The "Informatik Centrum Dortmund e.V." (ICD) was founded in 1989 as a spin-off company of the Computer Science department of the University of Dortmund, Germany. The Informatik Centrum Dortmund GmbH was founded in 2019. Today, ICD is available as a research and development partner for companies coming from different technological areas. ICD strives to improve and accelerate the transfer of current research results in computer science and information technology into industrial products.
The company
The product range of ICD comprises the provision of services related to Internet and Multimedia, the development of specialized software, the application of automatic picture classification, the optimization of complex systems, support for decision-taking using fuzzy logic as well as the development of educational software.
Due to its close contact with the Computer Science and Electrical Engineering Departments of the University of Dortmund, ICD has access to the latest results of current research. The settlement of projects at ICD is done according to industry standards.
ICD makes it easier for companies to take advantage of the broad know-how collected at the University of Dortmund through:
- joint application-centered development projects that are conducted at ICD;
- projects comprising research and development that ICD conducts for its customers;
- courses and tutorials that are being offered by ICD.
ICD considers itself a service provider supporting the realization of latest research results from the area of computer science and from computer applications into industrial products. Its goal is to provide access to the know-how, and also to researchers and graduates of the University of Dortmund, in particular for medium-sized companies in a fast und unbureaucratic way.

entityDescription:
Hasselt University (UHasselt) is a young, independent and innovative university, located in the center of Europe in Belgium. Today, Hasselt University counts seven faculties, four research institutes, three research centres, 6,522 students and 1,540 researchers and staff. 
The university is regionally anchored, has a pronounced regional, national and international orientation and is thus strongly committed to both the region and the world. As a civic university, UHasselt wants to deploy people and knowledge to tackle society’s major challenges, in full collaboration with regional, national and international others. The university is committed to take responsibility and share knowledge in ways that benefit the society. Students, staff, researchers and alumni are both able and willing to make the society smarter, more agile and better. Innovation is a constant in everything the university does. Today’s and tomorrow’s challenges guide teaching, research and social engagement of the university. Therefore, Hasselt University imparts its student knowledge, skills and insights in the world in order to make them critical, engaged global citizens, able to adapt to an ever-changing world. By breaking down the silos between research disciplines in the interdisciplinary research institutes and centers, scientists with a different scientific background can work better together on new answers to complex problems. To enhance knowledge on local, regional and global challenges, Hasselt University collaborates with other universities, research centres, governments, businesses and civil society organisations. The university also employs its networks to send students, staff and academics into the world and attract others to our region. About 17% of all PhDs are joint PhDs, about 42% of the PhD student at Hasselt University are from outside Belgium and 12% of the academic staff is international. This way, Hasselt University becomes a place where the region meets the world and the world meets the region. 
Hasselt University also strives pays a lot of attention to the creation of equal opportunities for women and men in research. A policy plan on gender issues has been developed which describes actions to ameliorate recruitment and promotion of both women and men and to improve the balance between work and family. It is therefore not surprising that Hasselt University was the first Flemish university to obtain the “HR Excellence in Research” label of the European Commission in 2011.
Hasselt University is ranked in the Times Higher Education Ranking in the 2018-2019 edition and is listed in the section 351-400. In the Times Higher Education Ranking of universities less than half a century old, Hasselt University is ranked as number 46.

entityName: Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development
entityDescription:
The Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development determines strategic directions, develops programmes and plans for sustainable development of society on green and cyclic economy policies with the aim of transforming Croatia into a prosperous, resource-efficient and competitive economy, while assuring climate neutrality, conservation and sustainable use of natural resources.
The Ministry's scope encompasses the development and improvement of the Croatian economy, the instruments and measures of economic policy; development of micro-, small- and medium-scale enterprises; industrial policy and the application of innovative and new technologies; management of the guarantee fund for the improvement of industry; jobs related to intellectual and industrial rights usage and the encouragement of innovation in industry and trade, aiming to develop the competitiveness of the Croatian economy; mining; easement and encouragement of subsidising and export.
The Ministry works in accordance with other governmental bodies to coordinate strategic use of state property, including participation in the coordination of restructuring and rehabilitation of legal entities, analysis of restructuring procedures of companies owned by Croatia and management of ownership shares of companies owned by Croatia; trade in the EU single market; supply and pricing; national coordination of activities within the EU single market, including technical legislation and quality infrastructure, coordination and development of national policy for standardisation, accreditation, compliance and measurement assessments; phenomena and the state of the market; protection of consumers; strategic goods stockpiles.
The Ministry conducts administrative and other duties pertaining to the development, improvement and coordination of the public procurement system; development and improvement of the concession system within its jurisdiction and supervision of its implementation and improvement of the public-private partnership system.
The Ministry conducts work pertaining to nature protection and conservation in accordance with the sustainable development policy of Croatia; jobs pertaining to waste management and environmental impact assessments; climate change mitigation and adaptation; water management and other energy-related jobs.
Protection of the environment is one of the most challenging activities that permeates through all aspects of human society. Through proclaiming the National sustainable development strategy, the Ministry became a point of coordination at the national level for subjects pertaining to sustainable development and the coordinating body for multilateral environmental agreements and global questions related to sustainable development on a global scale.
The Ministry conducts work related to Croatia’s participation in EU bodies in areas of its jurisdiction.
The Ministry also conducts other work that falls under its jurisdiction, as defined by law.

entityDescription:
Sorbonne University is a world-class research university, presenting the comprehensive disciplinary range of arts, humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, engineering and medicine. Sorbonne University is at the crossroads of diverse types of knowledge and capable of responding to the intellectual and scientific challenges of the 21st century.
The University offers its 55,600 students the best educational opportunities for the success of each of their personal and professional projects, through monodisciplinary, bi-disciplinary and interdisciplinary programs. Close to 10,200 of its students are international and 4,400 are in doctoral programs. With its three main faculties, it offers varied and original opportunities across disciplines and high quality research and training environment with, for instance, the largest university Library in France. 
Sorbonne University research draws on more than 3,400 professor-researchers and another 3,100 research partners from the major French research organisations, working side by side in more than 130 laboratories. In addition to Nobel Prizes, Fields Medals and other awards, the university has exceptional transdisciplinary institutes and is also theheadquarters for the European Marine Biological Resource Centre. With 8,500 publications per year (approx. 10% of all publications in France), Sorbonne Université is a major player in international knowledge and innovation economy. SU also receives the largest number of EU grants among French universities, with more than 150 awarded H2020 projects, including 40 MSCAs and 27 ERCs. With its research partners, a total of 97 H2020 ERC grantees have been hosted in Sorbonne University’s laboratories. 
Following its tradition in hosting excellent researchers from around the world, the university is engaged into the adoption of the European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers.
Sorbonne University is a member of the European University Association (EUA), the Network of Universities from the Capitals of Europe (UNICA), the International Alliance of Research Universities (IARU) and the League of European Research Universities (LERU).

entityDescription: Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań is the major academic institution in Poznań and one of the top Polish universities. Its reputation is founded on tradition, the outstanding achievements of the faculty and the attractive curriculum offered to students. In addition to its facilities in Poznań, it has campuses in Gniezno, Kalisz, Piła and Słubice/Franfurt-Oder. The University currently employs nearly 3,000 teaching staff, including 371 tenured professors and other professors with title, 1407 assistant professors, 369 senior lecturers and lecturers and over 2200 nonacademic employees. The University was founded in 1919 and currently its student population is nearly 40 000 students (nearly 700 are international students). Students may choose between 180 possible professional specializations. In recent years the educational offer has become increasingly diverse. New educational projects include: integrated studies in humanities, natural sciences, social sciences, and program carried out in cooperation with other institutions both in Poland and abroad. The mission of the University is to advance knowledge through high quality research and teaching in partnership with business, the professions, public services and other research and learning providers. The University is a center of academic excellence, where research and teaching are mutually sustaining, and where the context within which research is conducted and knowledge is sought and applied is international as much as regional and national. The University continuously extends and updates research programs and contents of study curricula, with special emphasis on their interdisciplinary and international nature. The University recognizes its role as a strategic partner in Central Europe, and therefore aspires to contribute to the region’s economic growth social development and environmental sustainability. The University prides itself on its achievements and aligns its principles with those of the Great Charter of European Universities. It promotes pro-European ideas and actively participates in the international academic community, seeks to implement joint research and educational programs. It aims to strengthen ties with the European Union Member States and embarks on new initiatives conducive to cooperation with the countries of Europe. In 2002-2018 our professors coordinated or were partners in more than 130 research projects funded by the European Union Framework Program (FP5, FP6, FP7 and Horizon 2020) and many other international research projects. AMU is a member of: EUA - European University Association, EUCEN - European University Continuing Education Network, The Compostela Group of Universities, The Santander Group - European University Network, European Chemistry Thematic Network and other European Research Networks. During the last 10 years, UAM has participated in 26 Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions projects (within FP7 and Horizon 2020: 8 individual, 4 ITN, 14 other) and 2 ERC projects (1 Consolidator Grant as a leader, 1 Advanced Grant as a member of the research group).

entityDescription:
As part of the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft, Fraunhofer IZM specializes in applied and industrial contract research. Fraunhofer IZM’s focus is on custom tailored packaging technology solutions and the integration of multifunctional electronics into systems with regard to functionality, costs and reliability.

The institute has a staff of more than 440 and saw a turnover of 37.6 million euros in 2020, of which 76 percent was earned through contract research and benefits from its close cooperation with the Technische Universität Berlin. Fraunhofer IZM assists companies and other institutes with application-oriented pre-competitive research, as well as the development of prototypes and small volume production. Our services include application advice, technology transfer and further qualification of personnel through practical training. In numerous R&D projects, ongoing skills and know-how are continuously being developed which can be passed also to SME-partners on a development stage.

Within Wafer Level System Integration IZM is specialized in developing advanced packaging and system integration technologies on all wafer sizes (100 mm to 300 mm) thus being able to offer customer-specific solutions for microelectronic products in the overall scope of smart system integration. This includes a broad cooperation network with manufacturer and users of microelectronic products as well as with cleanroom equipment producers and material developers from the chemical industry from all over the world. The interconnection technologies are offered on board, module and package levels and the integration of electrical, optical and power-electronic components and systems are at the forefront of the research. By simulating thermal and mechanical coupling and electrical, magnetic, electromagnetic phenomena at stages of the development process, IZM can compare the functionality and capacity of different technologies as early as during the concept design phase. The most important application areas are microelectronics and microsystem technology, RF and high-speed system design, photonic applications including fiber optics and power electronic systems. All technological developments are supported by environmental and reliability analysis reaching from nano-characterisation level to evaluation and optimisation at the system level until they reach market maturity with. Focus is on harsh environment applications like automotive, space and avionics.

description:
LIP is the reference laboratory for research in particle physics and related technologies in Portugal, and the Portuguese reference partner of CERN. The laboratory has nodes in Lisboa, Coimbra and Braga, closely collaborating with local universities. LIP has about 200 international members (100 PhD researchers), is an Associate Laboratory, and was rated as “Excellent” in the 2019 independent evaluation promoted by FCT, the Portuguese Agency for Science and Technology Funding. 
Growing increasingly multidisciplinary, LIP’s research includes a world-class fundamental research programme in particle and astroparticle physics, technological applications to healthcare, space exploration, information technologies and big data analytics. At the centre of LIP’s mission are also advanced scientific and technical training and a strong commitment to engaging society with science and community development. LIP collaborates at CERN, ESA, GSI, SNOLAB, SURF, Fermilab, and the Pierre Auger and SWGO observatories. 
LIP is part of several infrastructures in the FCT roadmap, namely the National Distributed Computing Infrastructure (INCD), ProtoTera, The Portuguese Association for Proton Therapy and Advanced Technologies for the treatment of Cancer, and the Brain Imaging Network. The laboratory offers all conditions and infrastructures for the successful implementation of the work plan: a mechanical workshop, laboratories and competence centers providing support to the research groups and offering high quality services to the community; outstanding computational facilities; administrative support; project management and communication offices; office space.
entityDescription: LIP (Laboratório de Instrumentação e Física Experimental de Partículas) is a technical and scientific nonprofit association created in 1986 by the ex-National Board for Scientific and Technological Research (JNICT) and the ex-Instituto Nacional de Investigação Científica (INIC), lately joined by the Associação Nacional dos Industriais de Material Eléctrico e Electrónico (ANIMEE). Following the reorganisation of the scientific public agencies in Portugal, the present sponsors of LIP are the National Foundation for Science (FCT), the Bureau for International Relations for Science and High Education (GRICES), both under the Ministry of Science and Higher Education, and ANIMEE. LIP was created when Portugal joined CERN as a full member-state and its main objective is the science and technology research in the field of experimental high-energy physics, associated instrumentation and computation. The science and technology activity of LIP takes place in the framework of international collaborations, aiming at the realisation of experiments, mainly in the European laboratory for particle physics, CERN, in Geneva, Switzerland. LIP does part of its job in Portugal (experiment conception, fundamental research on radiation physics and detectors, technology development and data analysis) executing at CERN or elsewhere all that concerns the direct preparation of experiments and data acquisition.

The Miguel Hernández University of Elche was established by the Generalitat Valenciana in 1996, and teaching activities began in the fall of 1997. The UMH, whose main campus is located in the city of Elche, operates 4 campuses in all: Altea, Elche, Orihuela, and Sant Joan d'Alacant. Its campuses extend over almost 95 hectares, there are 75 university buildings, and constructed areas cover about 210,000 m2. Currently, the UMH is home to 25,000 students, of which 13,000 are enrolled in official degree programs (bachelor, master, PhD), with the remaining 12,000 learning in continuing education programs. 
The Miguel Hernández University has 7 faculties (Faculty of Experimental Sciences, Faculty of Fine Arts, Faculty of Health and Social Sciences, Faculty of Medicine, Faculty of Pharmacy, Faculty of Social and Legal Sciences of Elche, and Faculty of Social and Legal Sciences of Orihuela) and 2 schools (School of Engineering of Elche and School of Engineering of Orihuela).
Regarding academics, the Miguel Hernández University of Elche offers 25 bachelor's, 53 master's, and 13 doctoral programs. In addition to these official programs, the UMH also offers hundreds of its own Continuing Education courses and programs, including University Expert, unique UMH Master's, Advanced University Diploma, University Specialist, Summer, Winter, Refinement, Bridging, university access, and language instruction, among others.
UMH employees include around 1,000 research personnel and teaching faculty, of which 550 are full-time and 450 are part-time. As for its researchers and faculty, 800 hold PhD's. There are around 500 university staff employees, and around 300 employees are contracted through projects.
To consolidate international presence and projection, the Miguel Hernández University of Elche maintains around 600 agreements with foreign universities, 350 with Spanish universities, and 20 agreements for joint degree programs with universities outside Spain.
